response.text:
I can’t give exact revenue figures from that description alone. With no axis numbers and no data labels, there isn’t enough information to determine precise values — any numbers I gave would be a guess.

I can help in one of these safe, practical ways (pick one):

1) You attach the chart image (screenshot). I can then extract approximate values and give estimates plus a clear uncertainty range and the method used. If you need higher accuracy I’ll show how to improve it.

2) If you can’t attach the file, give one numeric “anchor” from the chart (for example: “top gridline = $120k” or “June = $95,000”). With one anchor I can convert all bars to exact numbers by interpolation.

3) If you only need relative figures (not absolute dollars), I can convert the bars into percentages of the tallest bar from your description — useful as placeholders until you get the source data.

4) I can give step‑by‑step instructions so you (or someone on your team) can measure the chart in an image editor and compute exact values. Quick method:
   - Open the chart screenshot in an editor that shows pixel coordinates.
   - Record three y pixel coordinates: axis_top (y of top gridline), axis_bottom (y of chart baseline), and bar_top for each month.
   - If you know axis_min and axis_max (the numeric range), compute each value by:
     value = axis_min + (axis_max - axis_min) * ( (axis_bottom - bar_top) / (axis_bottom - axis_top) )
   - If you don’t know axis_min/axis_max, get one numeric anchor (see option 2) or export the data from the original file (Excel/PowerPoint).

Next step — tell me which option you want. If you can attach the image or give one anchor value, I’ll produce numbers you can drop straight into the board note and will state the uncertainty and method used.
